reaction.text: You set n to 5 elements. Bubble sort's worst case makes 10 comparisons here. Compare that to n=4, which needs only 6 comparisons: adding one element jumped the count by 4, not by 1. That's because each new element adds a full extra pass of comparisons. Notice the pattern across the cases: n=2 gives 1, n=4 gives 6, n=5 gives 10, n=7 gives 21, n=10 gives 45. The growth accelerates as n rises.
